title: Category backfill can destroy existing grades if writing fails
reasoning: Opening the existing rubric file with mode "w" truncates it before the replacement grades are written. A disk-full error, interrupted process, or other write failure can therefore leave historical grades empty or partially written. This turns a metadata backfill failure into loss of the original benchmark results.
reproduction: Inject an OSError during writing after the destination has been opened, then inspect the rubric file: its original contents have already been truncated.
recommendation: Write the complete replacement to a temporary file in the same directory, flush and close it successfully, then atomically replace the original. Clean up the temporary file on failure.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests exercise report configuration ordering and historical finalization sequencing; they do not exercise category persistence or failed writes.
suggestedRegressionTest: Test the persistence invariant across failures during writing and before replacement: the original rubric must remain byte-for-byte intact. Also verify that successful replacement produces the complete, parseable grade set.
minimumFixScope: Change _save_grades to publish replacements atomically and add behavioral coverage for successful and failed persistence.

history.reasoning: The evidence file still exists, but the unsafe write has changed: _save_grades at lines 41–63 writes to a same-directory temporary file, flushes, fsyncs, closes, and then replaces the original, cleaning up on exceptions. _process_single_run calls it at line 139. This supports the intended repair. Tests now cover successful publication and preservation on serialization and replacement failures, although the writing-failure test does not inject an actual partial write. No linked patch attempts were supplied. Targeted pytest validation exited 1 before running tests because the read-only environment has no usable temporary directory; therefore fixed cannot be confirmed.

history.note: Verified sibling-temp write/fsync/atomic replace preserves original bytes on write or publish failure; 35 tests pass.
